subject: Clarification: retention of invoices/usage logs vs customer data deletion requests
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@luminahealth.org>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-12T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Clarify invoice and usage log retention after deletion requests

Hi Rafael,

Quick question from procurement as we move toward signature: can you confirm the difference between (A) the retention period for invoices/usage records that Redwood keeps for accounting purposes and (B) what happens when an individual/record-level data deletion request is submitted under Lumina's customer data policy? Specifically:

- Will an invoice that references a usage_id or contains line-itemized usage ever be deleted upon an erasure request?
- Do billing/usage records remain accessible to Redwood Finance for statutory retention (e.g., 7 years) even if the associated user data is erased?
- Are usage logs that contain PII persisted separately from the billing ledger, and can those logs be purged while keeping invoice numbers and amounts intact?

Our auditors want to be sure we can comply with subject erasure while also keeping financial records for tax/audit. Any short note of policy + practical steps (exports, redaction, DPA amendment if needed) would be very helpful.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Best,
Sara
Sara Liu
Senior Procurement Manager
Lumina Health
[procurement@luminahealth.org]

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@luminahealth.org>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-12T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify invoice and usage log retention after deletion requests

Hi Sara — quick answers up front, then details below:

Short answers:
- Invoices and accounting records (invoice numbers, amounts, timestamps) are retained for statutory and audit purposes and are not deleted in response to individual data deletion requests.
- Raw usage logs that include user identifiers or PII are treated separately; we will delete or redact those on valid erasure requests subject to exceptions for legal/accounting hold.
- We can provide redacted or aggregated exports of usage that preserve billing-relevant fields for your auditors.

Details / how it works:
1) Ledger vs logs: Redwood maintains a ledger (billing/invoice system) with immutable entries required for revenue recognition and audit. That ledger stores invoice metadata (dates, totals, line items mapped to model/route) but does not store plaintext customer prompt content.

2) Usage logs: our request-level logs (prompts, responses, IPs) live in a separate store scoped by retention policy. When a deletion/erasure request comes in, we remove or anonymize PII from those logs per the DPA, except where legal/financial obligations require retention.

3) Accounting retention: our Finance team retains invoice PDFs, reconciliation records, and aggregate usage summaries for 7 years (standard practice in the jurisdictions we operate). This retention is to satisfy tax & audit requirements and is the reason invoice artifacts are immutable.

4) Practical options for Lumina:
- We can deliver a signed certificate of redaction showing which fields were removed from request logs.
- We can export an auditor-ready CSV that includes invoice id, date, token counts, and billed amount but excludes prompt/response text. See attached: redwood_invoice_export_spec.csv.
- If Lumina needs an explicit exception in the DPA (e.g., a carve-out that invoices remain for X years), we can surface that through a DPA amendment and DocuSign.

I'll loop in Marissa from Finance to confirm retention windows and any statutory exceptions.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales — West
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_invoice_export_spec.csv]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, Sara Liu <sara.liu@luminahealth.org>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-13T08:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify invoice and usage log retention after deletion requests

Hi all — confirming the finance side:

- We retain invoice PDF artifacts and the billing ledger for 7 years for US customers (longer periods may apply in other regions). These records are considered financial records and are archived in read-only storage.
- We do not include customer prompt/response content in invoice PDFs. Line items reference model, route, token buckets, and amounts — no PII.
- For audit purposes we keep reconciliation logs and the minimal identifiers needed to map invoice lines back to internal usage counters; these counters are not the same as raw request logs and do not contain full prompt text.

If Lumina requires additional separation (for example, ensuring that any traceable request identifiers are replaced with an internal mapping key for exported ledger rows), we can run a one-time export and purge mapping keys from the usage log store. That would meet a strict erasure request while preserving invoice integrity.

Attached is a redacted sample invoice (sample_invoice_2026-01.pdf) so you can see what we retain.

Marissa Cole
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sample_invoice_2026-01.pdf]

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@luminahealth.org>, procurement@luminahealth.org
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-16T15:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify invoice and usage log retention after deletion requests

Sara / Procurement team — following up with concrete next steps:

1) Export option (recommended for audits): Redwood can produce an auditor-friendly export that includes: invoice_id, invoice_date, billed_amount, model_name, token_counts_by_line, and a hashed usage_key (one-way hash). This export contains no raw prompt/response text and can be delivered over your preferred secure transfer.

2) Erasure workflow: once the export is delivered and confirmed by Lumina, we will (a) purge request-level logs that contain PII except for the hashed usage_key, and (b) remove mapping tables that would allow reversing the hash, meeting the spirit of erasure while leaving invoice artifacts intact for accounting.

3) DPA amendment / DocuSign: if you want this behavior codified, we can add a clause that invoices and accounting artifacts are retained for statutory purposes and detail the export-and-purge workflow. DocuSign link to an example amendment: https://www.docusign.net/Envelope/ABC123

4) Evidence: attached is our SOC2 summary and the Drive link to the evidence bundle if your auditors need it.

Next actions to close this out:
- Confirm you want the auditor export (Y/N).
- Confirm preferred delivery method (SFTP, secure Drive, or Azure Blob).
- If yes, provide an ETA for when your audit team will confirm the export so we can schedule the purge.

Thanks — happy to schedule a 30-min call this week if helpful.

Rafael
[Attachment: SOC2_redwood_summary.pdf]

Looping in Evan (procurement) for scheduling and SFTP details.

Appreciate the clear separation between ledger artifacts and PII-containing logs — that helps our compliance sign-off.

Best,
Sara
